The synthetic observation contains 421 Fourier samples over 21 station pairs from 7 stations, not 421 distinct physical baselines. Both calibrated and corrupted complex visibilities, noise estimates, 269 per-scan phases and 233 log-amplitude ratios are given. Original archive has 20 fields and no scan timestamps.

The supplied 64x64 reference matches the fixed make_ring_image formula within floating-point rounding. The Fourier operator uses 2 microarcsecond pixels, 128 microarcsecond field,descending half-pixel-centered coordinates,+2pi i phase and triangle-pulse response. Array display orientation is explicit; no celestial bearing is inferred.

All eight released Fourier matrices agree with the selected source operator within 1e-14 maximum error. Full forward, adjoint, dirty-image and PSF fixtures reproduce within 1.5e-13. Closure-loss values and gradients agree with retained ehtim parity fixtures at both stored test images to 1e-10 relative error.

NumPy 2.2.6/Accelerate emitted 177 floating-point matmul warnings despite finite results. Warnings are retained, all numeric input arrays are finite, and eight matrix-vector contractions agree with independent einsum computations within 2.23e-15. Warnings alone are not evidence of numerical failure.

forward_unit.npz declares 10 UV coordinates but stores 421 output visibilities. The first 10 match its declared operator and all 421 match the full observation operator. This is a fixture-contract inconsistency, not a valid 10-row test.

The standalone visibility_chisq helper returns 1.4113820493; the retained ehtim fixture returns 0.7056910246. The helper divides by M, while fixture and solver objective use 2M; gradients also differ by exactly 2. No scientific score is rewritten.

Gull-Skilling and simple entropy fixture values/gradients reproduce. TV fixture repeats the current implementation, but a fixed 2x3 directional finite difference is -2.95011335 while its source gradient gives +2.95011335. This reproduced sign defect affects that helper; the six main saved comparisons use gs/simple and are not invalidated solely by this test.

The small preprocessing functions reproduce their own fixtures but pick first matches across repeated station pairs: 35 triangles and 35 quadrangles, rather than the supplied 269/233 per-scan closures. Some resulting triangle UV sums are as large as 1.89e9 wavelengths; supplied per-scan triangles close within 2.14e-6. main.py uses the supplied per-scan arrays, avoiding this helper path.

A fixed deterministic station multiplier applied to the same released samples leaves computed triangle phases and quadrangle log ratios unchanged within 1e-12. This verifies gain cancellation algebra only. The released calibrated/corrupted observations came from noisy source calls; their wrapped phase RMS difference is 15.7676 degrees and log-ratio RMS difference 1.09991, so they are not an exact gain-only control.

All six metrics.json rows reproduce exactly with current visualization.py: flux-match to reference, range-normalized NRMSE and cosine NCC. The generator instead uses reference-RMS normalization, giving closure-corrupt NRMSE 1.0778 versus 0.1384. The metrics fixture likewise retains old RMS error 0.9156 while current helper yields 0.1176. Notebook outputs belong to differing historical computations and are not current reruns.

The live local dispatch uses generic unscaled range error. Saved corrupted closure-only gives NRMSE 0.114238 and cosine NCC 0.604421; visibility RML gives 0.130818 and 0.000107. Range error alone gives the zero-image control 0.128424. No task pass/fail thresholds exist; these are descriptive single-output comparisons.

The live reference is unit-sum ground_truth.npy, matching data/ground_truth.npz:image. The image_jy reference sums 0.6 and is the physical Jy/pixel version. Exact physical truth therefore gets NCC 1 and live NRMSE 0.051370 rather than zero. This is a normalization contract mismatch with the README label, not an imaging error.
